key_insight: At 12.5% La substitution in BaTiO3, enhanced electronic screening is linked to weaker ferroelectric polarization, lower static dielectric response, and reduced optical anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: Donor substitution offers a potential design lever for balancing polarization, dielectric response, and optical transparency in perovskite devices.
method: Density functional theory for lattice, electronic structure, and optical properties
Density-functional perturbation theory for phonons and dielectric response
evidence_signal: Calculations show reduced tetragonality and Born effective charges, polar-mode hardening, dynamical stability, and an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein–Moss-type mechanism.
watch_item: Results apply only to the modeled 12.5% La composition; additional concentrations are needed to establish quantitative doping trends.
paper_title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
